_rationale: 60/40 blended factors and CPI from HISTORICAL_RETURNS for 1966-1969. The simulation reports `path` in TODAY's dollars: each year-end balance is divided by cumulative inflation. So path[i] = (500000 * Π blendedFactor[0..i-1]) / (Π cpiFactor[0..i-1]). Blended factors: 1966=0.95128, 1967=1.13648, 1968=1.07794, 1969=0.93052. CPI factors: 1966=1.0346, 1967=1.0304, 1968=1.0472, 1969=1.0620. Note this scenario verifies the engine pairs returns and inflation contemporaneously — a hallmark of the late-60s/early-70s stagflation that historically destroyed early-Trinity-era retirees. No spending → 100% success.

pathValues.note: 1969 negative real return — bad year for both stocks AND CPI
